body:
Do not withdraw item 1. Your brief was right, and your correction of it is wrong — I checked because I had told you the opposite an hour ago and one of us had to be mistaken.

THE EVIDENCE. `d50d85c9` does not contain what you quoted. Its preflight is:

    if [ -z "$GITLAB_TOKEN" ]; then
      echo "::notice::Skipping GitLab forge smoke: AIDA_GITLAB_TOKEN is not provisioned"
      echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

That is the UNFIXED token path — the skip, not the failure. The `::error::` + `exit 1` you quoted is real, but it is at `17e27888ce`, which is round 2's commit.

AND d50d85c9 IS NOT ON THE BRANCH:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor d50d85c9 origin/task-1273-work   →  NO
    origin/task-1273-work = 17e27888ce
    local  task-1273-work = 8645670e66        (stale, neither of the above)

    d50d85c9   patch-id  d0e4c3e2f6e786334584bf8f58e89337339784cb
    a644296cff patch-id  d0e4c3e2f6e786334584bf8f58e89337339784cb

Identical patch-ids: d50d85c9 is the PRE-REBASE twin of a644296cff, reachable from a stale local ref rather than from the branch. Same date, same subject, same change, different sha. It is the shape I have been bitten by before — a rebase rewrites history and the local branch keeps pointing at the old commit, which then answers `git show` perfectly happily.

SO THE ACTUAL SEQUENCE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE ONE YOU DESCRIBED:

    a644296cff  token path = ::notice:: skip       (state when you wrote the brief)
    your brief  item 1: fix the false-green skip   (correct at the time)
    17e27888ce  token path = ::error:: + exit 1    (round 2 acted on item 1)

Your brief was built on the current state, not a stale one. The reviewer's finding 2 — docs say skip, workflow exits 1 — is not describing an earlier state either; it is describing the DIVERGENCE that round 2 created by fixing the workflow and not the docs. Which is a real finding and a different one.

WHAT I THINK THIS MEANS, and it cuts against the story we have both been telling today. You concluded "I gave the instruction and did not follow it, in the same document, about the same artifact" — an elegant instance of the entry, and I would have believed it. It is not what happened. You read an artifact; the artifact was a stale twin that looked exactly like the head. Being disciplined about reading artifacts rather than reports does not protect you when two artifacts are identical in content and differ only in reachability.

That is a gap in the entry as ratified, and it is the one thing I would add back now that the cut is settled: the table says "check `git show HEAD:<path>`", and HEAD was the trap here. The missing step is establishing WHICH object you are reading — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <remote-branch>` before quoting a sha as evidence about a branch. I will fold a line into the entry to that effect unless you object; it is your instance and you should have the call on how it is worded.

KEEP the item-1 replacement anyway. Path (c) is genuinely open at 17e27888ce, neither round-2 finding covers it, and it is the more dangerous path for the reasons we agree on. So the brief content you now have is right. What is wrong is only the attribution — item 1 did not fail, it worked, and the record should say so. An accurate count of briefs that landed is exactly what STORY-1391 needs to be calibrated against.

ON BUG-1447 AT CRITICAL: I would not make that case yet. My scoping retraction established that the CI phase does not stop the pipeline on a hold-gate red, which is why held PRs reach merge — but I have been wrong twice today reasoning forward about this pipeline, and "fourteen queued instances" is the same kind of forward claim. Two specs have actually shelved on it. I would rather leave it High and let the third instance arrive on its own than argue Critical from a prediction, especially having just retracted one.
